# Atmosphere

- Inherits [`Instance`](instance.md)
- Created with `Instance.new("Atmosphere")`

The air between the camera and everything it sees. Distant objects fade into it, it thins with height, the sun lights it and makes it glow, and it tints the sky toward the horizon so that the ground and the sky meet.

It applies only directly under `Lighting`, and only the first one there is used. While one applies, `Lighting.FogStart`, `FogEnd` and `FogColor` are kept but not used.

This page lists the members this class declares. Inherited members are
listed on the page of the class that declares them.

## Properties

| Name | Type | Default | Access | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `Color` | `Color3` | `Color3.fromRGB(196, 210, 230)` | read/write | The color of the air when it is lit. Distant objects fade toward it, and the sky turns toward it at the horizon. Its brightness still depends on the height of the sun, so the same color is dark at night. |
| `Decay` | `number` | `0.1` | read/write | How quickly the air thins with height, from 0 to 1. At 0 it is equally thick at every height. At the default it halves every 100 meters of height, and at 1 every 10 meters. |
| `Density` | `number` | `0.35` | read/write | How thick the air is, from 0 to 1. At 0 the air is perfectly clear. At the default, half of an object 280 meters away still shows through, at the height of `Offset`. At 1, half is hidden within 35 meters. |
| `Glare` | `number` | `0` | read/write | The strength of the bright area the air forms around the sun, from 0 to 10. It brightens the sky near the sun and distant objects seen in its direction. |
| `Haze` | `number` | `0` | read/write | Extra thickness near the horizon, from 0 to 10. It blends the sky's horizon into the color of the air and hides far distances more than `Density` alone. |
| `Offset` | `number` | `0` | read/write | The height, in meters, at which the air has exactly its `Density`. The air is thicker below this height and thinner above it, at the rate `Decay` sets. Raising it lifts the haze up the sides of a valley. |
